They are made from haloalkanes, amines and esters, and industrially by the oxo process, hydroboration and fermentation.

text: Let us recap. Alcohols are primary, secondary or tertiary, and Victor Meyer and Lucas tests tell them apart. They are made from haloalkanes, amines and esters, and industrially by the oxo process, hydroboration and fermentation. Distillation stops at ninety five point six percent. Hydrogen bonding gives high boiling points. Concentrated sulphuric acid dehydrates them to alkenes or ethers, depending on temperature. Dichromate oxidises primary and secondary alcohols, turning green. And esters form with water coming from the acid.
